source.doc: PESD5V0L1BA Low capacitance bidirectional ESD protection diode (Nexperia, product data sheet, 11 April 2023)

source.ref: General description p.1 ('very small SOD323 (SC-76) SMD plastic package'); Table 3 Ordering information p.2 ('SOD323 plastic, surface-mounted package; 2 leads; 1.3 mm pitch; 1.7 mm x 1.25 mm x 0.95 mm body')

value.note: Two leads, both cathodes: pin 1 K1 (cathode of diode 1) and pin 2 K2 (cathode of diode 2). The back-to-back arrangement is what makes it bidirectional, and it means the part has no polarity to get wrong on a signal line.

Reverse standoff voltage, stated as a maximum of 5 V at Tamb = 25 degC — an explicit VRWM row, unlike the USBLC6-2 where the figure has to be read from the leakage test condition. Reverse leakage at VRWM = 5 V is typ 0.01 uA / max 1 uA. So this part suits a 5 V or 3.3 V signal line but must NOT sit on anything higher.

source.ref: Table 1 Quick reference data, VRWM row, p.1; characteristics table IRM row, p.4

value.note: Clamping voltage is specified at two surge currents with a non-repetitive 8/20 us exponential-decay pulse per IEC 61000-4-5. Note how much higher the 15 A figure is than the USBLC6-2's 5 A figure (33 V versus 17 V): this device protects the line from destruction but lets a much larger voltage through, which matters when the downstream pin's own absolute maximum is only VDD + 0.5 V. Maximum peak pulse power is 500 W and differential resistance is 80 ohm max.

value.note: READ THIS BEFORE PUTTING IT ON A DATA LINE. The part is titled 'Low capacitance bidirectional ESD protection diode', but its diode capacitance is 75 pF typical at f = 1 MHz, VR = 0 V — roughly 21x the USBLC6-2's 3.5 pF maximum. 'Low capacitance' is relative to bulk TVS diodes, NOT to high-speed-grade protection. 75 pF on a USB 2.0 high-speed pair would wreck the signal; this device belongs on low-speed lines such as I2C, buttons, GPIO and power inputs. This is exactly the substitution the capacitance_pf slot exists to catch, and the reason a part name must never be trusted in place of its specification.

source.ref: Table 1 Quick reference data, Cd row, p.1; characteristics table Cd row, p.4

value.note: Protects ONE signal line, bidirectionally. A USB 2.0 port would therefore need two of these for D+/D- plus separate VBUS protection, versus a single USBLC6-2 — and even then the capacitance makes it the wrong choice there. ESD withstand is quoted up to 30 kV, IEC 61000-4-2 level 4, with IEC 61000-4-5 surge handling of IPPM = 15 A.
